## TL;DR

`buildIndex` and `buildIndexDetailedAsync` both walked all of `work/` recursively for task files, so the review reports that now live under `work/reports/<id>/review-<n>.md` were parsed as tasks. They have no `id` frontmatter, so every `repoos` command printed a "skipped N task file(s) with no `id`" warning, and the noise grew with every review pass. I taught `walkFiles` to skip an explicit set of non-task directories and derived that set from `reportsRootRelPath` in `src/core/report-paths.ts`, so the reports location is owned in exactly one place. Both the synchronous and asynchronous index builders use the same helper. A new test covers the report file being silent and an id-less hand-written task file still warning, and `repoos list` on this repo now produces no warning on stderr.

## Work and rationale

The task was deliberately small: one behavioral fix in `src/core/indexer.ts` plus a focused test, without changing the report format or location. The core defect was in `walkFiles`: it recurses into every directory under `<root>/<workDir>` and collects files matching `config.taskExtensions` (currently `.md`). Since `work/reports/<task-id>/` contains `review-<n>.md`, those files were read, parsed, found to lack `id`, and counted in `skippedTaskFiles`. Both `buildIndex` and `buildIndexDetailedAsync` duplicate that walk and the warning, so both needed the fix — patching only the sync path would have left the server's boot path warning.

The acceptance criteria explicitly asked to use `reportsWorkDir`/`report-paths.ts` rather than a hard-coded directory name. I chose `reportsRootRelPath(config)`, which returns `<workDir>/reports`, then joined it with `config.root`. That means a repo that renames its work directory or changes its report location stays correct without a second place to update. I added a `nonTaskDirs(config)` helper next to `walkFiles` so the intent — "bookkeeping directories that are never tasks" — is documented in code rather than buried in the loop.

`walkFiles` now takes an optional `ReadonlySet<string>` of absolute directory paths to skip, defaulting to an empty set. When it sees a directory in that set it does not recurse. This is cheaper and clearer than collecting every file and filtering afterwards, and it matches the task's wording that the indexer "skips the reports directory". The read-only set conveys that the walker does not mutate it.

One decision worth recording: I left the legacy `work/engineering-reports/<id>/` directory alone. Its files are `round-<n>.json`, and the task extensions in this repo are `.md` only, so the indexer never picks them up and they cannot trip this warning. Widening the skip to that path would have been harmless but is outside the task's scope, and the report-path module treats the legacy directory as read-only compatibility rather than an active writing location.

I also considered filtering on the file name (`review-*.md`) instead of the directory. That would be narrower but wrong in principle: any future report or notes format under `work/reports/` would reintroduce the warning, and it would couple the indexer to the review-file naming scheme. Directory-level exclusion states the actual rule: reports are bookkeeping, not tasks.

## Approaches tried

The first, most direct approach was a post-walk filter that dropped any path whose repo-relative form starts with `work/reports/`. It works, but it reads every report file before discarding it and hard-codes the directory name unless it calls into report-paths anyway. I discarded it in favor of directory-level skipping.

A second option was to give `buildIndex` a `taskDirs`-style option from configuration. That would be a broader API change, and there is no user-facing requirement for configurable task directories. The internal `nonTaskDirs` helper keeps the same single source of truth without expanding the public surface.

For tests, I added `src/ui-app/tests/indexer-skipped-files.test.ts`, following the existing `indexer-metadata.test.ts` style: build a temporary root, write task files, call `buildIndex` with `skipGit: true`, and spy on `console.warn`. I split it into three cases: report files alone are silent, an id-less `work/*.md` still warns with exactly one skipped file, and the async builder gets the same treatment. The async case matters because the server boot path uses `buildIndexDetailedAsync`; without it, a future refactor could regress only the path users see at startup.

## Challenges and blockers

There were no blockers. The main subtlety was that the `repoos` CLI runs compiled `dist/`, not the TypeScript source, and a fresh worktree may have no `dist/`. I ran `bun run build` before invoking `bun dist/cli/index.js list` so the verification exercised the new code rather than a stale build. I confirmed the absence of the warning by redirecting stderr to a file and checking it was empty; grepping for "skipped" in normal output was misleading because task titles themselves contain that word.

The scoped `repoos check` created the expected WIP checkpoint commit on the task branch (documented RepoOS behavior), which left the worktree clean. Remote validation ran the test suite while the local scoped run skipped it by design, so the local run reported the remote-tests step as skipped rather than failed.

## Key learnings

- The indexer treats any `.md` under `work/` as a task candidate; any new bookkeeping tree with Markdown must either be excluded by directory or live outside `work/`.
- Both index builders duplicate the walk and the warning. Fixes here should land in both, or be factored so they cannot drift.
- Report locations belong to `report-paths.ts`; deriving the skip set from `reportsRootRelPath` keeps a work-directory change from silently re-enabling the warning.
- When a warning's wording also appears in task titles, verify stderr directly instead of grepping combined output.
